Communication & Health Education

Health communication and health education — methods, media, the teaching process and evaluation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe elements of communication
  • Plan health education for a group
  • Use appropriate teaching methods
  • Evaluate health education

In simple words

Health education turns knowledge into action. It is a process where people learn to take responsibility for their own health — through information, practice and support.

Communication

Element Explanation
Source Sender with clear ideas and credibility
Message What must change in the learner
Channel Words, pictures, demonstration, actions
Receiver The audience — their language, literacy and beliefs
Feedback Does the learner understand and act?
  • One-way communication: lecture, notice, radio — little feedback
  • Two-way communication: discussion, counselling — important feedback
  • Barriers: language, deafness, blindness, illiteracy, shy audience, wrong timing, distrust, unsigned matter

Health education process

  1. Assess needs: what the family already knows and believes
  2. Define the changes to be achieved
  3. Select the audience, content and media
  4. Implement in the language and setting of the learner
  5. Reinforce with practice and follow-up
  6. Evaluate: knowledge, behaviour and outcome

Teaching methods

Method Best for
Lecture Large groups, new information
Demonstration Skills such as handwashing or ORS preparation
Group discussion Attitude change and problem solving
Role play Sensitive topics like family acceptance
Flip charts, posters Low-literacy groups and clinics
Puppetry and street plays Illiterate and rural audiences
Radio and television Wide reach
Counselling Individual change

🔴 Two-way beats one-way

Choose discussion, demonstration and role play over lecture. People believe what they practise, not what they are told.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Communication has source, message, channel, receiver and feedback.
  2. Health education includes information, motivation and practice.
  3. Always assess the audience literacy and language first.
  4. Demonstration is best for teaching skills.
  5. Evaluation looks at knowledge, practice and outcome.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Barriers: language, blindness, deafness, illiteracy, distrust, wrong timing.
  2. Group discussion changes attitudes; lectures add knowledge.
  3. Flip charts and posters suit low-literacy audiences.
  4. Repeat the message through several channels for reinforcement.
  5. Health education should be planned with the community, not for it.

📌 Memory trick

Good health talk: P-P-R — Present the need, Practise the skill, Praise the change.

60-second revision

  • Communication elements: source, message, channel, receiver, feedback.
  • Process: assess, plan, teach, reinforce, evaluate.
  • Methods: lecture, demonstration, discussion, role play, media.
  • Two-way methods are more effective than one-way.
  • Match language, literacy and culture of the audience.

Test yourself

Which is a two-way communication method?

Answer: B. Group discussion allows immediate feedback and clarification; the others are one-way.

The best method to teach handwashing is:

Answer: B. Demonstration followed by return demonstration ensures the skill is actually learned.

Which is a common barrier to health education?

Answer: B. Illiteracy is a major barrier; use pictures, demonstration and role play instead of written material.

Health education is best evaluated by:

Answer: B. Evaluation looks at change in knowledge, behaviour and the health outcome.

A lecture is most appropriate when:

Answer: C. Lectures efficiently give new information to large groups but do not change attitudes or teach skills.
